drug_class: Histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor — a type of targeted cancer medicine
purpose: Vorinostat is used to treat a type of skin cancer called cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), specifically when the disease affects the skin and other treatments have not worked. It helps control the cancer and relieve uncomfortable skin symptoms like itching and redness. Your doctor has prescribed it because it is the right option for your specific situation.
how_it_works: Inside cancer cells, there are proteins that help control how genes are switched on or off. Vorinostat blocks certain proteins called histone deacetylases, which causes the cancer cells to stop growing and eventually die. Think of it like putting a brake on the cancer cell's ability to multiply and survive, while mostly leaving normal cells alone.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, tiredness, loss of appetite, and a change in taste. You may also notice dry mouth, hair thinning, or weight loss. Some people feel dizzy or have muscle aches. Most of these can be managed, so let your care team know if they bother you.
warnings: Vorinostat can cause serious blood clots in the legs or lungs — tell your doctor right away if you have leg swelling, pain, or sudden shortness of breath. It can lower your blood cell counts, increasing infection risk and causing anemia. It may also cause abnormal heart rhythms, low potassium or magnesium levels, and high blood sugar. Drink plenty of water to stay hydrated. Do not take it if you are pregnant, and use reliable birth control. Always tell your pharmacist about all other medicines you take, as interactions can occur.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg taken by mouth once a day with food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not open, crush, or chew them. Take it at the same time every day, and drink at least 2 liters of water daily to help reduce side effects. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember the same day, but skip it if it is almost time for your next dose.
